categories.title: Purple LEDs (violet 390-420 nm, purple/pink phosphor and red+blue bi-die, UV-A 365-385 nm)
categories.recommendation: Violet: TUOZHAN S2-2835UVTA-0.2W (C2827317, 2835, 390-400 nm, 705k stock) for glow/fluorescence effects; for a visibly purple pixel use GL0603PU01 (C51933300) or a red+blue bi-die XL-1615SURUBC (C965836) mixed by PWM.
notes: No datasheet among the violet/UV/purple parts gives an IEC 62471 risk group; they carry only generic 'do not look into the LED' warnings.  The 2835 parts emitting 45-220 mW at 365-400 nm should be treated as eye hazards at close range (diffuse or shield them, keep them out of direct view of a child).

The 'purple' parts rated in mcd at 5 mA (Vf ~2.6-3.1 V) behave like phosphor-converted purple/pink emitters (no datasheet gives a spectrum); the violet InGaN parts (Vf ~3.0-3.6 V) look dim and deep-violet because the eye's photopic sensitivity at 400 nm is only ~0.04 % of its 555 nm peak, yet their 45-180 mW of radiant power makes fluorescent inks and glow-in-the-dark pigments light up strongly.
None of these LEDs is Basic or Preferred.
